proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable in a short series; can trade off with I-to-H transition and recovery rates, potentially yielding similar fits with different internal trajectories and some split-to-split variability.
proposals.rationale: Anchor template: directly maps the target (weekly hospitalization rate) to an explicit hospitalization compartment, reducing phase/lag sensitivity versus delayed infection proxies and aligning with surveillance semantics. Keeps delay at 0 for robustness across rolling splits and avoids extra SEIRS complexity.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May blur interpretation by attributing hospitalization-rate signal partly to I, risking amplitude bias (over/under-shooting peaks) if the series is primarily admissions-driven rather than combined burden.
proposals.rationale: Alternative hospitalization-linked mapping that can be more robust if admissions reflect a mixture of current infectious burden and hospitalized census/flow; may reduce sensitivity when H alone is noisy or under-identified while still keeping delay=0.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Residual phase mismatch if true lag varies over time; may compensate via parameter tradeoffs (incubation vs infectious duration), causing instability across rolling splits.
proposals.rationale: Secondary comparison branch: simpler than SEIRS and uses a short 1-week observation lag to capture plausible admission delay without over-lagging moderate peaks; intended to improve temporal alignment while limiting instability seen with longer delays.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can still over-lag around moderate peaks in some splits, leading to systematic timing errors and increased sensitivity to initialization/parameter coupling.
proposals.rationale: Short-lag alternative to test whether a 2-week delay better matches admissions timing for this age group while still respecting the constraint to avoid delay=3; maintains parsimony and avoids SEIRS reinfection dynamics.
